name: Chip supply
summary: Nexperia and STMicro warn AI demand is squeezing mature-chip supply for carmakers; no TSMC or Samsung stoppage
state: At the Electronica fair in Munich on 9–10 Nov, Nexperia's interim chief executive said the company was oversubscribed and STMicroelectronics' chief executive said he saw many bottlenecks, as suppliers shift capacity towards AI data centres and away from mature chips used in cars and industrial equipment (The Star; GM Authority, 10 Nov). Searches on 18 Nov found no TSMC or Samsung stoppage and no new controls halting a major supply chain, so shortages in a key segment keep Watch.
for_you: Chip bottlenecks tend to show up first as longer lead times for new cars, electronics and industrial equipment, rather than as empty shelves.
rubric_hit: Watch: shortages reported in key segments (mature automotive chips, 10 Nov); no major TSMC/Samsung disruption

sources.title: The Star — Chipmakers warn AI demand is creating bottlenecks in automotive supply chain
GM Authority — Chipmaker CEO warns AI demand creating automotive supply chain bottlenecks

why: Advanced chips underpin everything from phones to AI to weapons; supply is concentrated in Taiwan and Korea.
drivers: Export controls, Taiwan risk, fab outages, AI demand, materials.

rubric.alert: Major disruption to TSMC/Samsung output, or controls halting a major supply chain.
rubric.watch: New export controls, shortages reported in key segments, or a fab outage.
rubric.normal: Supply normal; no new major controls.
